## `150-090-dense-inclusion`

**Verified:** if J and K satisfy the local domination hypotheses and I′ is the band generated by J ∪ K, then I′ is contained in the ambient downward closure of K.

The downward closure of K is order-convex and contains K. Definition (85) supplies J ⊆ downward-closure(K), so it also contains J ∪ K. By the defining minimality of the generated band, it contains I′. This agrees with (87): every element of I′ lies between some j ∈ J and k ∈ K, hence lies below k.

Because K ⊆ I′, its closure relative to I′ is I′ intersected with its ambient closure, therefore all of I′. Thus relative density gives a relative equality. It does not give ambient equality: the already-recorded example 0 < 1 < 2, J = {1}, K = {2} has I′ = {1,2} and ambient closure(K) = {0,1,2}. The proof does not select either alternative of the manuscript's uncertain equality/inclusion sign.

## `150-095-comparability-dense`

**Verified refinement:** under the preceding density and faithfulness assumptions, comparable indices imply nonempty intersection of their pro-neighborhoods.

Use the neighborhood interpretation already stated in the 095 notes: the intersection is nonempty when every pair of open neighborhoods of the two strata meets. Write A_i = X_i*. If i ≤ j, faithfulness gives a point a ∈ A_i. Monotonicity and density give A_i ⊆ X_i ⊆ X_j = closure(A_j). An arbitrary open neighborhood U of A_i therefore meets A_j. Every open neighborhood W of A_j contains that meeting point, so U ∩ W is nonempty. The case j ≤ i is symmetric. Consequently no neighborhood-intersection stage is empty.

For a given ordered pair, the argument needs only nonemptiness of the lower stratum and density of the upper stratum in its closed stratum. The full local density-and-faithfulness assumptions supply both. Metrizability is unnecessary for this reverse implication; the page's separate metric/separation hypothesis for the forward direction is not discarded. This check does not assert the reverse implication from faithfulness alone or alter the literal caption.
